tEn: Why AI Has DHH Working 16-Hour Days
tZh: 为何 AI 让 DHH 每天工作 16 小时
sEn: DHH explains why the age of agents makes Linux the only viable OS and how AI is reshaping software development.
sZh: DHH 解释为何智能体时代让 Linux 成为唯一可行的操作系统，以及 AI 如何重塑软件开发。

consensus.en: macOS and Windows are unfit for the age of agents; Linux's terminal, config files, and error messages are what agents love.
consensus.zh: macOS 和 Windows 不适合智能体时代；Linux 的终端、配置文件和错误信息正是智能体所喜欢的。

consensus.en: Agents can now modify the OS directly, making the entire system malleable and deeply intoxicating for users.
consensus.zh: 智能体现在可以直接修改操作系统，使整个系统变得可塑，让用户深度着迷。

consensus.en: Open source and open weights are essential to keep frontier labs honest and prevent a duopoly.
consensus.zh: 开源和开放权重对于保持前沿模型实验室的诚信和防止双头垄断至关重要。

consensus.en: Software development difficulty has dropped to near zero; anyone who can steer agents can replicate top apps.
consensus.zh: 软件开发难度已降至接近零；任何能驾驭智能体的人都能复制顶级应用。

consensus.en: Human taste and vision still matter for the last 2% of perfection, but that may not last forever.
consensus.zh: 人类的品味和愿景对于最后 2% 的完美仍然重要，但这可能不会永远持续。

consensus.en: We may have true superintelligence in software development by next year, but embodied AI will take longer.
consensus.zh: 到明年我们可能在软件开发领域拥有真正的超级智能，但具身 AI 需要更长时间。

contrarian.en: Anyone who thinks source code provides a moat is delusional; even millions of lines won't protect ecosystems.
contrarian.zh: 任何认为源代码能提供护城河的人都是妄想；即使数百万行代码也无法保护生态系统。

contrarian.en: Apple risks becoming the AOL of the agent era by locking down its ecosystem and restricting agents.
contrarian.zh: 苹果通过锁定生态系统和限制智能体，有成为智能体时代美国在线的风险。

contrarian.en: Linux can overtake macOS in desktop market share within three years, possibly even twelve months.
contrarian.zh: Linux 可能在三年内，甚至十二个月内，在桌面市场份额上超过 macOS。

contrarian.en: The AI safety community's focus on worst-case scenarios leads to AI psychosis; we should focus on building.
contrarian.zh: AI 安全社区对最坏情况的关注会导致 AI 精神病；我们应该专注于建设。

contrarian.en: Most programmers' anxiety about AI is understandable but misplaced; we must lean into the change.
contrarian.zh: 大多数程序员对 AI 的焦虑可以理解但方向错误；我们必须拥抱变化。

contrarian.en: The return of pseudo-anonymous hacker culture and demo scene aesthetics is revitalizing computing.
contrarian.zh: 伪匿名黑客文化和演示场景美学的回归正在振兴计算技术。

turns.en: David, thank you so much for joining us. We're going to talk about all things company building, AI, software. Everybody knows you—I know you, Lenny's a huge fan—but would you mind giving a rough sketch of your background? Ruby on Rails, Basecamp, Hey, and your current projects.
turns.zh: David，非常感谢你来参加。我们要聊聊公司建设、AI、软件等所有事情。大家都认识你——我认识你，Lenny 也是你的超级粉丝——但你能不能简单介绍一下你的背景？Ruby on Rails、Basecamp、Hey，还有你现在的项目。

turns.en: Sure. I'm David Heinemeier Hansson. I've been building things for the internet, software, for about 30 years. About 23 of those with Basecamp—the original project management tool, SaaS before it was called SaaS, released the day before or after Facebook went live. That became the founding application for Ruby on Rails. Ruby on Rails was extracted out of that and was then used to build Twitter, GitHub, Shopify, Airbnb, Coinbase, and a million other applications. I've continued to work on both ever since. We sell Basecamp—that's version five now. Ruby on Rails is up to version eight. Five years ago we released hey.com, our email service. In those 25 years or so I wrote four books including Rework and Remote. I've been developing my voice around how to run a company and what I think about technology, and I put a lot of those thoughts onto X every day. Oh, and what am I doing now? I'm doing a Linux distribution called Omachi, the first native OS for the age of agents.
turns.zh: 好的。我是 David Heinemeier Hansson。我从事互联网软件构建大约 30 年了。其中大约 23 年是在做 Basecamp——最初的项目管理工具，在 SaaS 这个词出现之前就是 SaaS，发布在 Facebook 上线的前一天或后一天。它成了 Ruby on Rails 的创始应用。Ruby on Rails 是从中提取出来的，后来被用来构建 Twitter、GitHub、Shopify、Airbnb、Coinbase 以及无数其他应用。我一直在这两个项目上工作。我们销售 Basecamp——现在是第五版。Ruby on Rails 已经到了第八版。五年前我们发布了 hey.com，我们的电子邮件服务。在大约 25 年里我写了四本书，包括《重来》和《远程工作》。我一直在围绕如何经营公司和我对技术的看法发展自己的观点，每天把很多想法发到 X 上。哦，我现在在做什么？我在做一个叫 Omachi 的 Linux 发行版，第一个为智能体时代打造的原生操作系统。

turns.en: I love it.
turns.zh: 我喜欢。

turns.en: And we're having a lot of fun with that, getting hundreds of thousands of people to switch from Windows and Mac to a Linux system to finally make the prophecy come true after 25 years that this is the year of Linux on the desktop.
turns.zh: 我们玩得很开心，让数十万人从 Windows 和 Mac 切换到 Linux 系统，终于让 25 年后的预言成真：今年是 Linux 桌面之年。

turns.en: What was your first Linux distro?
turns.zh: 你第一个 Linux 发行版是什么？

turns.en: It was Ubuntu, and it was only two and a half years ago if we're talking about the desktop. I've been using Linux on the server since the '90s. But I did not run Linux on the desktop. I was a Mac head. Since 2001 I switched to beta four, I believe, of OS 10. And then just stayed in that ecosystem right up until Apple drove off the rails and got addicted to easy service revenue where you could just take 30% of other people's business. That is a great business to be in. You don't even have to innovate. You can waste 10 years developing a car you never sell to anyone. You can launch a huge flop of a ski mask. No one cares if you can just take 30% of other people's business, you're golden. Well, what was not golden about that was their relationship to developers. I was certainly one of those developers who had been advocating for Apple for decades. Suddenly, finally I had enough and I switched to Linux.
turns.zh: 是 Ubuntu，如果谈桌面的话，那只是两年半前的事。我从 90 年代起就在服务器上使用 Linux。但我没有在桌面上运行 Linux。我曾是 Mac 铁粉。从 2001 年起我切换到 OS 10 的 beta 4，我相信是 beta 4。然后一直留在那个生态里，直到 Apple 偏离正轨，沉迷于轻松的服务收入，直接抽走别人业务 30% 的流水。那是一门好生意。你甚至不需要创新。你可以花 10 年开发一辆永远卖不出去的车。你可以推出一款彻底失败的滑雪面罩。只要你抽走别人业务 30% 的流水，就没人管你，你就赢了。但不赢的地方在于他们与开发者的关系。我当然是那些几十年来一直为 Apple 辩护的开发者之一。突然，我终于受够了，转向了 Linux。

transcript.sec: Why Linux for the Age of Agents

turns.en: Is that your big why for Linux desktop happening now? How much of it is Apple and Windows muddying the waters of their ecosystems versus AI and new technology that lets you modify the OS? I was playing with it last night and it's really remarkable what you can do. You just tell your agent modify the OS on which I'm operating right now and it does it and it works. It's amazing.
turns.zh: 这就是你认为 Linux 桌面现在能成的大原因吗？其中有多少是 Apple 和 Windows 在搅浑自己的生态，多少是 AI 和新技术让你能修改操作系统？我昨晚玩了一下，你能做到的事真的很了不起。你只要告诉你的智能体修改我现在操作的这个操作系统，它就能做到，而且有效。太神奇了。

turns.en: That's what's making Linux happen in a big way. All of these other motivating factors like Apple not being so nice to developers is something a few developers care about, not even all of them. Plenty of them just continued to suffer the abuse because that's what you've got to do if you sell commercial software—you have to be on the App Store. So I don't think that was ever going to motivate droves of people to switch to Linux, but the age of agents absolutely positively will. And there was just another drop today that Apple is making it even harder to use macOS with agents, even more scary pop-up screens about how you shouldn't let Claude have access to your files. Well, what is it going to do then if it doesn't have access to your files? So Omachi is going in a very different direction. We are leaning all in. The entire operating system is being developed by agents for the past 5 months or so now, maybe even 6 months. I've not written a single line of code for Omachi by hand, but I've written hundreds of thousands of lines of code through agents. And we're using that to accelerate the development of Omachi itself and we're creating things at a rate I scarcely believe would be possible. And then we're putting all that power into the hands of users. And I think, exactly as you had, anyone who gets the experience where the entire operating system is malleable—they can change anything, they can change how any element of it works, they want a new start menu, they want to move the clock around, they want a different calendar, they just want to add a feature to an existing part of the operating system—and they can just do that by prompting and it literally happens in sometimes maybe at most a few minutes, is deeply intoxicating. And I don't think any of those people, if they really soak in it for 5 minutes, are going back. So I'm extremely bullish on the idea that both macOS and Windows are just unfit for the age of agents. And I think the age of agents is going to be the only thing that matters when it comes to these computers in about 5 minutes. So we're really just leaning hard into the idea that operating systems we've had for 40 years built around mouse and click dynamics, they just don't work for the age of agents. Let me give you just one basic example. If you want to remap the hotkeys to go to a different workspace in macOS, there's only one way to do that. Manually go into a settings app, click one field at a time, put in the new hotkey, then click the next field, then put in that hotkey.
turns.zh: 这就是让 Linux 大规模成真的原因。其他那些动机因素，比如 Apple 对开发者不够友好，只有少数开发者在意，甚至不是全部。很多人继续忍受这种虐待，因为如果你卖商业软件，你就必须上 App Store。所以我不认为那能促使大批人转向 Linux，但智能体时代绝对会。今天又有一个消息，Apple 让用智能体操作 macOS 变得更难，弹出更吓人的屏幕，说你不该让 Claude 访问你的文件。那如果它不能访问你的文件，它还能干什么？所以 Omachi 走的是完全不同的方向。我们全力投入。整个操作系统在过去大约 5 个月，甚至 6 个月里，都是由智能体开发的。我没有为 Omachi 手写一行代码，但我通过智能体写了数十万行代码。我们用这个来加速 Omachi 本身的开发，创造东西的速度连我自己都几乎不敢相信。然后我们把所有这些能力交到用户手中。我想，就像你刚才说的，任何人一旦体验到整个操作系统是可塑的——他们可以改变任何东西，可以改变任何元素的工作方式，想要新的开始菜单，想移动时钟，想要不同的日历，只想给操作系统的现有部分加个功能——他们只要提示一下，有时最多几分钟就真的实现了，这会让人深度上瘾。我不认为那些人，如果真的沉浸 5 分钟，还会回去。所以我极度看好这个观点：macOS 和 Windows 都不适合智能体时代。我认为在大约 5 分钟后，智能体时代将是这些计算机唯一重要的东西。所以我们真的在全力押注这个想法：我们用了 40 年、围绕鼠标点击动态构建的操作系统，就是不适合智能体时代。让我给你一个基本例子。如果你想在 macOS 中重新映射热键以切换到不同的工作区，只有一种方法。手动进入设置应用，一次点击一个字段，输入新的热键，然后点击下一个字段，再输入那个热键。

turns.en: You cannot do that agentically. Well, I guess you can have computer use to it, but that's pretty dumb. That's pretty silly. And what we have on the Linux side is that every single thing that made Linux hard to use in the past—oh, it's very terminal heavy, it's got a bunch of config files that's hard to figure out, and it's got inscrutable error messages—these are the three things agents love. They want a command line interface for everything. They want predictable config files that they can just edit and update. They want all the details in the error messages. So all these historic deficits for Linux have literally this year turned into the reason why you want Linux on your computer if you're into agents, if you're into AI. And at this point, who that's making anything is not into agents, is not into AI.
turns.zh: 你不能以智能体式的方式做到那一点。好吧，我猜你可以用 computer use 来实现，但那很蠢。那很傻。而在 Linux 这边，过去让 Linux 难用的每一件事——哦，它非常依赖终端，有一堆难以理解的配置文件，还有晦涩难懂的错误信息——这些正是智能体喜欢的三件事。它们想要每个东西都有命令行界面。它们想要可预测的配置文件，可以直接编辑和更新。它们想要错误信息里包含所有细节。所以所有这些 Linux 的历史缺陷，今年真的变成了你想要在电脑上装 Linux 的理由，如果你对智能体感兴趣，如果你对 AI 感兴趣。而到了现在，谁做东西还不关注智能体、不关注 AI 呢？

turns.en: So I think Apple is running the risk right now of becoming the AOL of the agent era. We're going to provide this walled garden. We have Genmoji over here. You do not need to use an actual agent from an actual Frontier Lab. Just give us a chance to give you something watered down and protected. And most people don't want AOL. They want the open internet. And is what we're trying to give them with the Omachi.
turns.zh: 所以我认为 Apple 现在正冒着成为智能体时代的 AOL 的风险。我们要提供这个围墙花园。我们这边有 Genmoji。你不需要使用来自真正前沿实验室的真正智能体。就给我们一个机会，给你一些稀释过的、受保护的东西。而大多数人不想要 AOL。他们想要开放的互联网。而这正是我们试图用 Omachi 给他们的。

transcript.sec: Mobile's Duopoly and the Opening for a Third OS

turns.en: What happens to mobile in this world?
turns.zh: 在这个世界里，移动端会发生什么？

turns.en: Mobile has to change the same way. And this is actually one of the reasons why I am so excited about this age of agents. First on the desktop because the window is now open for a third operating system for the first time in 25 years. The last time we had an opening was that OS X in 2001. That was the last time anyone premiered a new operating system that made any dent in the global market share. Since then, nothing. Window closed. This year, window open. Suddenly Linux has a chance again in a way it literally hasn't had for 25 years. Mobile has been suffering under the same setup. We've had a duopoly and Google and Apple have just divided that juicy 30% revenue from everyone else's business between them. And what were you going to do? Microsoft tried. They spent, I don't know, several billion dollars to make Windows OS a thing on mobile and it wasn't a thing in huge part because they did not have the applications. Who wanted to switch to a Windows phone if they couldn't get Instagram? So that died on the vine. That's what's changing right now. We're seeing it already on Linux. Someone in the Omachi community rewrote the only application I still kept a Mac around to run, Adobe Lightroom, because it had all my plugins and it had all my presets for my cameras and I just wasn't willing to give that up so I had like a Mac just for that, right? One guy over the course of like two weeks replicated all of Lightroom. Not just replicated but made it better than Adobe had literally spent, I don't know, a decade and a half and tens of millions of dollars if not more developing. Now apply that to a phone, an operating system running on a mobile device that suddenly can get every app you'd ever want because if it does not exist, someone is going to come up with it because they can just vibe code it in five minutes. That completely changes the game. The entire lock on these ecosystems is about application availability. And in the age of agents, software development has just dropped to zero in terms of pricing, in terms of difficulty. Anyone, not even software developers, anyone who can steer these agents can replicate something as good as an Adobe, as good as anyone. That's a completely reset of the playing field. And that's why this can happen. So my motto right now is first we take Manhattan, desktop, then we take Berlin, mobile.
turns.zh: 移动端也必须以同样的方式改变。而这实际上是我对智能体时代如此兴奋的原因之一。首先是在桌面端，因为 25 年来第一次为第三个操作系统打开了窗口。上一次我们有机会是在 2001 年的 OS X。那是最后一次有人推出新的操作系统并在全球市场份额中占有一席之地。从那以后，什么都没有。窗口关闭了。今年，窗口打开了。突然之间，Linux 又有了机会，这是它 25 年来从未有过的。移动端一直在同样的格局下受苦。我们有一个双头垄断，Google 和 Apple 把来自其他人业务的诱人 30% 收入瓜分了。你打算怎么办？微软试过了。他们花了，我不知道，几十亿美元让 Windows OS 在移动端成为现实，但它没有成功，很大程度上是因为他们没有应用。如果拿不到 Instagram，谁想换到 Windows 手机？所以它夭折了。这就是现在正在改变的事情。我们已经在 Linux 上看到了。Omachi 社区里的某个人重写了唯一一个我还留着 Mac 来运行的应用程序——Adobe Lightroom，因为它有我所有的插件和相机的所有预设，我就是不愿意放弃，所以我有一台 Mac 就为了这个，对吧？一个人在大约两周的时间里复制了整个 Lightroom。不只是复制，还做得比 Adobe 花了，我不知道，十五年、几千万美元甚至更多开发出来的还要好。现在把这个应用到手机上，一个运行在移动设备上的操作系统突然可以得到你想要的每一个应用，因为如果它不存在，就会有人把它做出来，因为他们可以在五分钟内 vibe code 出来。这完全改变了游戏规则。这些生态系统的全部锁定就在于应用可用性。而在智能体时代，软件开发的定价和难度都降到了零。任何人，甚至不是软件开发者，任何能驾驭这些智能体的人都能复制出和 Adobe 一样好、和任何人一样好的东西。这完全是重新洗牌。这就是为什么这能发生。所以我现在的座右铭是：首先我们拿下曼哈顿，桌面端；然后我们拿下柏林，移动端。

transcript.secZh: 移动双寡头与第三OS机会

turns.en: Well, it is fascinating because like the concept of building a third mobile ecosystem 5 years ago was it was just I mean it's certain to fail, completely daunting. And now for some token budget we can replicate the top 10, 100,000, 10,000 apps. And for many apps they may not even need to be replicated because the agents can just natively do the work that you're signing the app up to do.
turns.zh: 嗯，这很迷人，因为就像五年前建立第三个移动生态系统的概念，那只是——我是说它肯定会失败，完全令人望而生畏。而现在用一些 token 预算，我们就能复制前 10、100,000、10,000 个应用。对于许多应用来说，它们甚至可能不需要被复制，因为智能体可以直接原生地完成你注册应用要做的工作。

turns.en: Correct. I think that's really interesting too because one thing is to replicate say Adobe Lightroom or Adobe Photoshop. That's always been the historical example, right? Linux was never going to succeed because it did not have like three apps. It did not have Microsoft Word, it did not have Adobe Photoshop and a couple of other things. Now, first of all, when was the last time I opened a word processor? I just asked my agent to come up with the contract and then I'll review it in markdown and when I'm happy I'll just have it make a PDF. That looks amazing. So I've been setting up the Amacon Foundation which is the nonprofit behind Omachi. We've raised, I don't know, $23 million in tokens and donations and I've had to make a lot of contracts. Every single one of those contracts made by an agent were no word processor was involved. I don't even sign my documents anymore. I just look it over and say that's good to go, sign it. And the agent has my signature and it'll put it on the document and then it will mail it out. So I don't go through word processor anymore. I don't need Word anymore. The same thing with photos. You want something changed about your photo, make this look great. What, you're going to spend tens of hours, hundreds of hours learning the intricacies of Photoshop? No one's going to do that. They're going to ask their agent to do it, and the agent's going to do a phenomenal job so that your photo comes back looking amazing. Or you want to remove someone in that photo, you just say like, hey, remove that idiot over there on the left. I just want to look at these two people. Boom. So I think the agents they're going to just eradicate entire classes of applications because these applications historically, especially something like Photoshop, was not just an application, it was a profession. It was something you had to learn and spend in some cases years getting good at. Now that's all great, but agents have taken all that on, and now they can do it without the app. But then even if you do want the app, what I've noticed and what I've seen happening in the Emacs community a lot already is that whenever you need something of a word or you need something of a Photoshop, you can on the fly basically just make this happen.
turns.zh: 没错。我觉得那也很有趣，因为复制比如 Adobe Lightroom 或 Adobe Photoshop 是一回事。这一直是历史上的例子，对吧？Linux 从来不会成功，因为它没有那三个应用。它没有 Microsoft Word，没有 Adobe Photoshop，还有另外几个东西。现在，首先，我上次打开文字处理器是什么时候？我直接让我的智能体起草合同，然后我用 Markdown 审阅，满意了就让它生成 PDF。看起来很棒。所以我一直在筹建 Amacon 基金会，这是 Omachi 背后的非营利组织。我们已经筹集了，我不知道，2300 万美元的 token 和捐款，我不得不签很多合同。每一份由智能体制作的合同都没有涉及文字处理器。我甚至不再亲自签署文件了。我只需看一眼说可以了，签吧。智能体有我的签名，它会把它放在文件上，然后寄出去。所以我不再经过文字处理器了。我不再需要 Word 了。照片也一样。你想对照片做点什么，让它看起来很棒。什么，你要花几十小时、几百小时学习 Photoshop 的复杂功能？没人会那样做。他们会请他们的智能体来做，智能体会做得非常出色，让你的照片回来时看起来很棒。或者你想去掉照片里的某个人，你只需说，嘿，把左边那个白痴去掉。我只想看这两个人。砰。所以我认为智能体会直接消灭整类应用，因为这些应用在历史上，尤其是像 Photoshop 这样的东西，不仅仅是一个应用，它是一种职业。那是你必须学习、有时要花几年才能精通的东西。现在这一切都很好，但智能体已经承担了所有这些，现在它们可以在没有应用的情况下做到。但即使你真的想要应用，我注意到并且在 Emacs 社区已经看到很多的是，每当你需要某种文字处理或某种 Photoshop 功能时，你基本上可以当场就把它做出来。

transcript.sec: The Speed of AI and Real-Time Creation

transcript.sec: The Future of Software Mutates Live

turns.en: Everything just mutates live. There was such a preview of what the future of software is going to be. Everything is just going to mutate live. And that's 1,500 tokens a second. We can do that today. What's going to happen next year? What's going to happen 2 years from now when these models are going to run at 100,000 tokens a second and a million tokens a second? So directionally we're going towards a place where all these historic barriers for anyone to launch and succeed with a new ecosystem is just going to disappear.
turns.zh: 一切都在实时变化。这就像是未来软件形态的一次预演。一切都将实时变化。而这是每秒 1,500 个 token。我们今天就能做到。明年会发生什么？两年后，当这些模型每秒能跑 10 万个 token、100 万个 token 时，又会发生什么？所以从方向上看，我们正走向一个地方：任何人要推出并成功运营一个新生态系统的历史性壁垒，都将彻底消失。

turns.en: Because not only can the ecosystems be created far more easily. I mean, Omachi, the current version that we have was made over the course of about two and a half months part time, me and Ryan Hughes, my main partner on this project. That was the version that turned into this thing that's now taking off like crazy. What? We're competing against thousands of programmers over at Microsoft, tens of thousands of programmers around the world working at these huge companies, and now suddenly a slapdash handful of people can make something that's not just competitive but superior. That's completely unheard of. That was never going to happen before.
turns.zh: 因为不仅生态系统的创建变得容易得多。我是说，Omachi，我们现在的这个版本，是我和这个项目的主要搭档 Ryan Hughes 利用业余时间、花了大约两个半月做出来的。就是那个版本变成了现在这个疯狂起飞的东西。什么？我们在和微软的数千名程序员竞争，和全世界这些大公司里的数万名程序员竞争，而现在突然之间，随手凑起来的几个人就能做出不仅具有竞争力、而且更优越的东西。这完全闻所未闻。这在以前绝不可能发生。

turns.en: Now, you look at venture capital, right? Like there's literally a what? Two decade long history where all the money just plowed into developers because you needed developers to build the thing and you also needed a runway of several years to have these developers build things. Now suddenly all of that is getting compressed down to days, weeks, at worst months. And that's with the models we have right now. Just in the time I've been developing Omachi, we went from, um, whatever, Opus 4.8 was what I started this new phase of it. And it was good. And then we got Sonnet and now we got Opus 5.5. turns.zh: 现在你看看风险投资，对吧？ literally 有长达二十年的历史，所有钱都砸向开发者，因为你需要开发者来构建东西，而且你还需要好几年的跑道让这些开发者把东西做出来。现在突然之间，这一切都被压缩到几天、几周，最坏也就是几个月。而这还是用我们现在的模型。就在我开发 Omachi 的这段时间里，我们从，呃，随便吧，Opus 4.8 是我开启这个新阶段时用的版本。它很好。然后我们有了 Sonnet，现在又有了 Opus 5.5。Opus 4.8 到 5.5 之间的差距是巨大的。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: And are we going to get another drop before Christmas? Probably. And if not, then we're going to get it early next year. And these hops are accelerating. turns.zh: 圣诞节前还会不会有新版本发布？很可能有。如果没有，明年初也会有。而且这些跳跃在加速。所以任何仍然认为源代码里有护城河——哪怕是几百万行代码——或者认为那能保护他们生态系统的人，都是在自欺欺人。

turns.zh: 正是如此。我觉得我能把自己的品味、自己的愿景、自己的完美主义更多地注入软件，因为我发现某个地方不太对、差了几个像素、想要修复它，这之间的障碍已经崩塌了。我现在看到任何问题，任何问题，任何不完美的软件，都有机会从问题走向完美。这就是我现在每天工作 16 个小时的原因。

I don't even want to return to the assembly line work world where an auto worker in Detroit could make a decent living by putting things monotonously together by hand. I don't think we should return to that. We got to lean forward into it. We got to find a way to bring everyone along into that.
turns.zh: 现在，你完全可以既抱有这种同理心，又说：对，我不会回到前工业时代。我不会在这里用自己的锄头和牛搞自给农业。那不是我想回到的世界。我甚至不想回到那个流水线工作的世界——底特律的汽车工人靠单调地手工组装东西就能过上体面生活。我不认为我们应该回到那种状态。我们必须向前倾，必须找到一种方法让所有人都跟上。

turns.en: And some of that is vibes. Some of it is vibes. And right now there is a battle of the vibes. And in that battle, you have a bunch of people who for whatever reason, maybe their own personal anxieties, which can be very real, and sometimes also just sort of finds this audience where like I'm going to be the anti-AI person here. And there's not just one, there's like a billion of them. Whole communities actually are getting addicted to this stuff.
turns.zh: 其中一部分是氛围。一部分是氛围。而现在正有一场氛围之战。在这场战斗中，有一群人，不管出于什么原因——也许他们个人的焦虑非常真实，有时也只是找到了这个受众群体，说“我要在这里当反 AI 的人”。而且不止一个，有十亿个。整个社区实际上都对此上瘾了。

turns.en: If you draw the Venn diagram with the most insufferable woke people with blue hairs and the anti-AI people, it's a circle, right? So in some ways we are replaying the last round. We're replaying every battle ever because that's how the law lines are now drawn up. And I think unfortunately the way for them, that is, the way this cookie crumbled was that the people they didn't like leaned into this first. And that left them only one position to take, which was the opposite. And therefore they had to become an anti-AI people, right?
turns.zh: 如果你画一个维恩图，把最令人难以忍受的蓝发 woke 人士和反 AI 人士放在一起，那就是一个圆，对吧？所以某种程度上我们在重演上一轮。我们在重演每一场战斗，因为现在的战线就是这样划的。我认为不幸的是，对他们来说，事情就是这样定局的：他们不喜欢的人先拥抱了这件事。这让他们只剩下一个立场可站，那就是对立面。因此他们不得不成为反 AI 的人，对吧？

turns.en: So I mean, I do think there's a beautiful irony in there because there's a bunch of those insufferable people. I don't mind at all having a bit of anxiety about the future here, right? A bunch of the rest of it. I had quite some anxiety about the future about five years ago when they seemingly had all the cultural power and could cancel anyone anytime, any place. Now, the shoe's a little different, isn't it?
turns.zh: 所以我的意思是，我确实认为这里面有一种美妙的讽刺，因为有一堆那样令人难以忍受的人。我完全不介意对未来有一点焦虑，对吧？其余的大部分。大约五年前，我对未来相当焦虑，当时他们似乎掌握着所有文化权力，可以随时随地取消任何人。现在，情况有点不同了，不是吗？

turns.en: But not all of it. And we shouldn't kind of fall into that trap that it's all just going to be tribal and there's this side or the other side or that everyone who is uncomfortable with AI is a blue-haired idiot. It's just that every blue-haired idiot is also anti-AI.
turns.zh: 但不全是。我们不应该掉进那个陷阱，认为一切都只是部落式的，要么这边要么那边，或者每个对 AI 感到不安的人都是蓝发白痴。只是每个蓝发白痴也恰好反 AI 而已。

turns.en: But getting to sort of bring them along and to realize or help them realize that, you know what? You can feel about this whichever way, but there is only one way forward and that's through. We're not going back. No one is going to willingly give up this technology ever unless we end up as paper clips on a stack somewhere in AI warehouse. We're not giving this up. This is here now. The world is just different as it was so many other times before. After the Wright brothers flew, the world was different. We're not going to ship everything with boat and so forth.
turns.zh: 但要带着他们一起走，并让他们意识到或帮助他们意识到：你知道吗？你可以对此有任何感受，但前进的道路只有一条，那就是穿过它。我们不会回头。没有人会自愿放弃这项技术，除非我们最终变成 AI 仓库里的一堆回形针。我们不会放弃这个。它已经在这里了。世界就是不同了，就像之前许多其他时候一样。莱特兄弟飞行之后，世界就不同了。我们不会再用船运一切等等。

turns.en: So, we have this obligation to push in. And who I look to in that is first all my fellow travelers in this. I mean, as you mentioned, Carmack or Tim Sweeney or Mitchell Hashimoto or there's a million of these people I deeply respect who've worked on software products that I've been using my entire career. 100% of them are leaned in. They're piled.
turns.zh: 所以，我们有义务推进。在这方面，我首先看向所有同行者。我的意思是，正如你提到的，Carmack 或 Tim Sweeney 或 Mitchell Hashimoto，或者有无数这样的人，我深深尊敬他们，他们开发的软件产品我整个职业生涯都在使用。他们 100% 都投入了。他们堆进去了。

turns.en: Then I also look to this really curious phenomenon that's been happening in both the Linux world but also in the AI world, the return of the pseudo-anonymous hacker. Now, the security world has always had this, but now it's leaking into the mainstream. On the Omarchy core team and the Omarchy Foundation staff list, we have pseudo-anonymous people. One, outfoxed, a creator of Quickshell, the malleable shell that we're using for all the desktop interactions, and Hand Core, one of the artists in there, which to me is a total throwback to the 90s and like phreaker culture, elite message boards, and all this stuff.
turns.zh: 然后我还看到一种非常奇特的现象，既发生在 Linux 世界，也发生在 AI 世界：伪匿名黑客的回归。安全界一直有这种现象，但现在它正渗入主流。在 Omarchy 核心团队和 Omarchy 基金会员工名单上，我们有伪匿名人士。一个是 outfoxed，Quickshell 的创造者，我们用于所有桌面交互的可塑 shell；还有 Hand Core，其中的艺术家之一。对我来说，这完全是 90 年代和电话飞客文化、精英留言板等等的回归。

turns.en: And I love that. I love that we have this energy around computers again, like it was in the 90s. The 80s were hackers and experimenters are suddenly at the forefront of everything because maybe that was true for a split second with the internet, and then the internet got commercialized. And then it got taken over, and we got platforms, and we got social media, and then it was dead. There was none of that anymore, right? It didn't last that long as sort of this free spirit.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这一点。我喜欢我们再次拥有这种围绕计算机的能量，就像 90 年代那样。80 年代是黑客和实验者突然站在一切的前沿，因为也许在互联网时代有那么一瞬间是真的，然后互联网商业化了。然后它被接管了，我们有了平台，有了社交媒体，然后它就死了。再也没有那些了，对吧？作为一种自由精神，它并没有持续那么久。

turns.en: Local AI, for example, has a ton of this stuff, too. 0x0 is someone we sponsor through the Omarchy Foundation. Mia's Lab also both pseudo-anonymous. 0x0 is, I guess, his identity is known, but goes by a handle. I love this energy that now individuals, thanks to the power of AI, can actually play a pivotal role in the forward progression of the industry because, as I said, once the internet got sort of bottled up and commercialized, a lot of the sort of frontier work to push things forward just got gobbled up by the big companies.
turns.zh: 例如，本地 AI 也有大量这种现象。0x0 是我们通过 Omarchy 基金会赞助的人。Mia's Lab 也是伪匿名的。0x0 我想他的身份是公开的，但用化名。我喜欢这种能量：现在个人， thanks to AI 的力量，实际上可以在行业的前进中发挥关键作用，因为正如我所说，一旦互联网被封装和商业化，许多推动事情向前的前沿工作就被大公司吞掉了。

turns.en: Oh, you had Google doing Chrome, and then that was your only browser in town. And then to create another browser was basically impossible. After the Linux kernel, the browser engine is the most complex piece of software humanity has ever produced. So we just closed off all these domains of the consequential bits of the computer, and only the biggest companies in the world could work on them. And now we're re-democratizing it. We're returning it to the hacker culture. We're returning it to the individual who can actually move some of this stuff forward.
turns.zh: 哦，你有了 Google 做 Chrome，然后那就是城里唯一的浏览器。然后创建另一个浏览器基本上是不可能的。在 Linux 内核之后，浏览器引擎是人类有史以来生产的最复杂的软件。所以我们就把计算机中所有重要领域的这些领域都关闭了，只有世界上最大的公司才能研究它们。现在我们正在重新民主化它。我们正在把它还给黑客文化。我们正在把它还给能够真正推动其中一些事情前进的个人。

turns.en: So I look to those people, basically anyone doing cool with a pseudo-anonymous handle online are like, hey, hey, I got to follow this person. Something's going on over here. I love that. It's like it's anti-LinkedIn culture. Anti-LinkedIn culture is what it is, right? It's just the complete opposite. And a big part of it is infused by X.
turns.zh: 所以我看向那些人，基本上任何在网上用伪匿名化名做酷事的人，我都会想：嘿，嘿，我得关注这个人。这边有事情在发生。我喜欢这一点。这就像是反 LinkedIn 文化。它就是反 LinkedIn 文化，对吧？完全相反。其中很大一部分是由 X 注入的。

turns.en: X has played such an enormous connecting tissue role for this whole revolution, for the artist, for the pseudo-anonymous hackers, for the local AI movement. It's all getting connected through X in a way that if those blue-haired bandits had somehow managed to hold on to that back before Elon brought it, we might not have had any of it at all. It might all have ended up being LinkedIn in human slop.
turns.zh: X 在这场整个革命中扮演了巨大的连接组织角色，对于艺术家、伪匿名黑客、本地 AI 运动都是如此。一切都通过 X 连接起来，如果那些蓝发强盗在埃隆买下它之前设法保住了它，我们可能根本不会有这一切。它可能最终都变成 LinkedIn 的人类泔水。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: I just want I just very very quick throwback also. Another thing that I loved you remember demo culture in the '90s?
turns.zh: 我只想非常非常快地回溯一下。另一件我喜欢的事，你还记得 90 年代的 demo 文化吗？

turns.en: Oh my god, yes.
turns.zh: 哦我的天，是的。

turns.en: Dude, it is so back in the creative aspects of AI. It's amazing. Like some of the most sophisticated demos are by like these random, you know, artists that have no interest actually in like, you know, building businesses is purely for the love of art. And I don't remember the last time we had such a movement and it's awesome.
turns.zh: 老兄，它在 AI 的创意方面完全回来了。太棒了。就像一些最复杂的 demo 是由这些随机的，你知道，艺术家做的，他们实际上对建立企业没有兴趣，纯粹是出于对艺术的热爱。我不记得上次我们有过这样的运动是什么时候了，这太棒了。

turns.en: I'm trying to pull all of that into Omarchy.
turns.zh: 我正在努力把这一切都拉进 Omarchy。

turns.en: So, I don't know if you've tried Amachi yet, but one of the signature visual effects is the screensaver. And the screensaver is literally ASCII art running through 40 demo effects. Just looking totally out of a 1995 demo party intro, right? We're pulling all of those effects into it, keeping that terminal aesthetic, which is by the way also completely different aesthetic from Mac OS or from Windows because I think Linux historically a lot of the distributions thought if we would just make a TUI version of Windows, everyone would love us. No. No one wants a cheap copy of something that wasn't that great to begin with. They want something bespoke. They want something unique. And the aesthetic of Amachi is totally '90s demo culture. Totally that. That's exactly the kind of vibe that I'm going for.
turns.zh: 我不知道你有没有试过 Amachi，但它的标志性视觉效果之一就是屏保。那个屏保其实就是 ASCII 艺术跑过 40 种 demo 效果，看起来完全像是 1995 年 demo party 的开场，对吧？我们把所有这些效果都融进去了，保持那种终端美学——顺便说一句，这和 Mac OS 或 Windows 的美学也完全不同，因为我觉得 Linux 历史上很多发行版都以为，只要我们做一个 Windows 的 TUI 版本，大家就会爱我们。不，没人想要一个本来就不怎么样的东西的廉价复制品。他们想要定制的、独特的东西。而 Amachi 的美学完全是 90 年代 demo 文化，完全就是那种感觉。那正是我想要的那种氛围。

turns.en: In fact, just before we hopped into this call, I am working on some how to set up local AI on your own machine. And one of the things we have is booting a local AI model can take a while, like I don't know, a few seconds, maybe in some cases even a few minutes. So while it's loading, I jammed in another ASCII effect, just like cool characters floating around on the screen. Does it have any functionality? No. Absolutely not. It's just there to make you feel like I'm using a cool ass computer because that's what the '90s and demo culture felt to me. Like I was into pirated games at the time too, and all these pirated games would have this intro cracked by Razor 1911 or whatever, and the text would swirl around. And I just felt a little cooler, a little cooler that day that I got to witness that.
turns.zh: 其实就在我们开始这次通话之前，我正在写一些关于如何在你自己的机器上设置本地 AI 的内容。其中一件事是，启动本地 AI 模型可能需要一段时间，比如几秒钟，有时甚至几分钟。所以在加载的时候，我塞进了另一个 ASCII 效果，就是酷炫的字符在屏幕上漂浮。它有什么功能吗？没有，绝对没有。它只是为了让你感觉自己正在用一台很酷的电脑，因为这就是 90 年代和 demo 文化给我的感觉。我当时也迷盗版游戏，所有这些盗版游戏都会有 Razor 1911 之类的破解开场，文字会旋转。那天我目睹了那个，就感觉自己酷了一点，酷了一点。

turns.en: I mean, BBS culture was like that too.
turns.zh: 我是说，BBS 文化也是那样的。

turns.en: Like that.
turns.zh: 就是那样。

turns.en: If you even if your goddamn job is pushing an Excel spreadsheet around, at least you feel alive for that hot moment while Machintosh is booting.
turns.zh: 就算你他妈的工作只是摆弄 Excel 表格，至少在 Macintosh 启动的那一瞬间，你感觉自己还活着。

turns.en: Yeah, like BBS culture was like that too, you know? I mean, all the protocols, you remember X modem, Y modem, Z modem, Kermit? Why is it Kermit? No one knows, but it seems badass.
turns.zh: 是啊，BBS 文化也是那样的，你知道吧？我是说，所有的协议，你记得 X modem、Y modem、Z modem、Kermit 吗？为什么叫 Kermit？没人知道，但听起来很酷。

turns.en: I ran an elite bulletin board system out of my bedroom. Three lines in, I was 14 years old. I can tell you when the guy from the Danish telecom monopoly showed up to install the third line and he saw this 14-year-old kid, was like, what the hell is going on here? This got to be illegal. And he was totally right. It was totally illegal. It was totally awesome. And I can still hear the US Robotics modem sound, the 33.6 connecting. It's just such an iconic sound, and we got to have more of that. Computers should be a little mysterious. They should be a lot of cool, and they should not be so polished. As much as I love Apple, I think Jonathan Ive essentially aluminum polished all character out of the computer in that regard. And maybe that was good for a time, but that time is over. We're getting the hackers back.
turns.zh: 我在自己的卧室里运营过一个精英 BBS，三线接入，那时我 14 岁。我可以告诉你，当丹麦电信垄断公司的人来安装第三条线时，他看到这个 14 岁的孩子，那表情就像：这到底是怎么回事？这肯定违法。他完全正确。那完全违法。那也完全酷毙了。我还能听到 US Robotics 调制解调器的声音，33.6 连接的声音。那真是一种标志性的声音，我们需要更多这样的东西。电脑应该有点神秘感，应该很酷，不应该那么精致。尽管我很爱 Apple，但我认为 Jonathan Ive 在这方面基本上用铝把电脑的所有个性都打磨掉了。也许那在一段时间内是好的，但那个时代已经结束了。我们要把黑客们带回来。

turns.en: David, you're such a legend, man. We really appreciate everything that you're doing now and everything that you've done. So we really appreciate you coming on and enjoy the conversation.
turns.zh: David，你真是个传奇。我们非常感谢你现在所做的一切以及你过去所做的一切。我们真的很感激你能来参加节目，也很享受这次对话。

turns.en: Thanks so much, David.
turns.zh: 非常感谢，David。

turns.en: It is always a pleasure to talk about the '90s demo culture, hackers, and cool.
turns.zh: 谈论 90 年代 demo 文化、黑客和酷东西总是很愉快。

turns.en: Let's do more together, man. What a pleasure.
turns.zh: 我们以后多合作，伙计。太愉快了。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: Where are you based in?
turns.zh: 你常驻在哪里？

turns.en: In person next time.
turns.zh: 下次当面聊。

turns.en: By the way, is the office real? Is the office real like the picture of your beautiful office view?
turns.zh: 顺便问一下，那个办公室是真的吗？就像你那张漂亮的办公室景观照片一样，是真的吗？

turns.en: It's very real. I'm not in that office right now, otherwise I would pan the camera around, but yes, that office is in Malibu and it never gets old. I mean, this is why I keep posting that picture just for my own satisfaction. Like I cannot believe I work here. And yeah, one of the spoils of capitalism. This office was brought to you by commercial software. Think of it.
turns.zh: 非常真实。我现在不在那个办公室，否则我会把镜头转一圈，但没错，那个办公室在马里布，永远不会腻。我是说，这就是为什么我一直发那张照片，只是为了自我满足。我简直不敢相信我在这里工作。是啊，资本主义的战利品之一。这个办公室是由商业软件赞助的。想想看。

turns.en: And really appreciate this. Really appreciate the time.
turns.zh: 真的很感谢。非常感谢你抽出时间。

turns.en: Thank you.
turns.zh: 谢谢你。

turns.en: Thanks so much.
turns.zh: 非常感谢。

turns.en: Thank you for having me on. Let's do it again in person.
turns.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。我们下次当面再聊。
百分之百。

turns.en: Good. Take care, man. Bye-bye. Happy hacking.
turns.zh: 好的。保重，伙计。拜拜。快乐黑客。

turns.en: All right.
turns.zh: 好的。
